subject: Re: Admin sprint — seed access & API key pinflow
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@helixhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: engineering-ops@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial admin seats + API key flow questions

Thanks Evelyn — excited to get started. A couple quick things from our side before the kickoff tomorrow: 

1) We expect ~12 admin maintainers across Prod and Staging (mix of SRE + Platform PMs). Will you be seeding seats or do we invite and map roles?
2) For API keys: do you recommend one service key per environment (prod/stage) or a single key with scopes? Our security team leans towards narrower scope/service keys.
3) Any constraints on IP allowlists / VPC egress we should prepare for?

If you can drop the seed template ahead of the call that'd be great. 

— Samir
Senior Platform Engineer, HelixHealth

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial admin seats + API key flow questions

Samir — thanks. Quick answers ahead of tomorrow's 10:30 kickoff: 

- Seat seeding: Redwood can seed admin seats from the CSV you provide; we normally seed a "workspace-admin" role and a smaller set of "billing-admin" seats. If you prefer invite-by-email we can do that too; seeding speeds up rollout. 
- API keys: our best practice is one service key per deployment role (prod-read/write, staging-read/write) — separate keys per environment make rotation and audit cleaner. We'll also attach scopes.
- Network: for hosted deployments you can either use IP allowlist for service-to-service calls or create a VPC egress rule for on-prem/private customers. We'll send the IP ranges and the VPC connection checklist.

Attached: "helix_admin_seed_matrix.csv" (template), a short runbook PDF with the seed cadence, and a service-keying text file with recommended scopes. 

I copied Jonas (implementation lead) and Monica (CS manager) — Jonas will coordinate the technical handoff and Monica will track acceptance criteria. Agenda for tomorrow's call attached at top of runbook. 

See you then,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_admin_seed_matrix.csv (csv template), initial-tenant-runbook.pdf (3 pages), service-keying-instructions.txt

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@helixhealth.com>

Thanks — got the template and runbook. A couple follow-ups after I'm reviewing with security: 

• Our security policy requires HSM-backed keys for any production service keys. Is that supported or can we store keys in our KMS and reference them?
• We also need an audit log export for admin-seat changes (CSV or syslog). What fields are in your audit events?

Samir will attach our initial CSV with the 12 names by end of day. If there are any fields you require in the seed file other than name/email/role, call them out and we'll extend the CSV.

— Alicia
Product Operations Manager, HelixHealth

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@helixhealth.com>; Samir Rao <samir@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Admin sprint — seed access & API key pinflow (implementation plan + next steps)

Alicia / Samir — following up after the kickoff and our security sync. Summary + concrete next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

1) Seed CSV accepted — we received 12 names for Prod and 6 for Staging. Monica will confirm the final set in HubSpot.
2) HSM/KMS: Redwood hosted supports customer KMS references for service keys (we do not store raw key material in plaintext). For HSM-backed keys you'll provide the KMS ARN and we'll configure key reference in the tenant. Action: Samir to share KMS ARN (due 2026-07-17).
3) Audit logs: Redwood can export admin-change events to an S3 bucket or a syslog endpoint. Events include timestamp, actor email, action (invite/role-change/seed/delete), target account, and request-id. Action: Alicia to confirm preferred export and retention (due 2026-07-19).
4) IP ranges & VPC checklist: Evelyn attached the IP ranges in the runbook; engineering-ops to confirm any additional egress needs.
5) Service key strategy: We'll create four scoped service keys: prod-write, prod-read, stage-write, stage-read. Each key will have a separate rotation window (90 days for staging, 30 days for prod). Action: Redwood to provision initial keys and hand them via ephemeral token exchange.

Acceptance criteria (what we consider "done"): 
- All admin seats seeded or accepted invites (12 prod, 6 staging)
- KMS/HSM reference configured for prod keys
- Audit export validated (one-week sample)
- Test generation from prod-write key returns expected latency < 120ms 95th pct in our sandbox test

I've dropped the implementation checklist into the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.team/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix-onboard (see file "implementation-checklist.md"). Monica will open the onboarding ticket in HubSpot and set milestones.

If anything above is off, call it out here. Otherwise we'll move to the provisioning sprint next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: implementation-checklist.md (Drive), helix_admin_seed_matrix.csv (received), initial-tenant-runbook.pdf
